    Injectivity of Ψ (Proposition 7.6) #

    "If Ψ[μ] = 0, change the arrows to remove the errors. They give a functor from C ⊗ k[ε]/(ε²) to the Hom category of the lifted modules reducing to the identity. […] On the actual projective corner it trivializes the algebra deformation with leading identity, so [μ] = 0."

    A functor C ⊗ k[ε] → (lifted modules) reducing to the identity is recorded by its ε-part: a derivation δ of C into the k-linear maps between evaluated modules with (rs φ, δ φ) a lifted map for every φ. We build δ on paths (δp), extend it linearly to the path category (δL), show that it kills the mesh ideal once the mesh errors vanish (δL_ideal), and descend it to C (δC).

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.

                          ∃ (H : (CatAlg.Alg D.F0)ᵐᵒᵖ →ₗ[k] (CatAlg.Alg D.F0)ᵐᵒᵖ), (∀ (p : ℤ) (a : (CatAlg.Alg D.F0)ᵐᵒᵖ), (galgA0 D hfin).gr.IsHom p a → (galgA0 D hfin).gr.IsHom (p + ↑q) (H a)) ∧ μ = GExt.hcobdry H

                          Proposition 7.6, injectivity: if Ψ[μ] = 0, then μ is the coboundary of a map of degree q.
